name: Eastern Plaguelands
summary: Scourge blight darkens the Eastern Plaguelands. Stratholme remains an undead stronghold, while the Scarlet Crusade fortifies the east. Light's Hope Chapel offers neutral refuge to those who fight back.

sections.title: A Land in Ruin
sections.body:
Once called the Eastweald, the Eastern Plaguelands were Lordaeron's fertile heartland. Stratholme anchored the region, with prosperous towns like Darrowshire and Corin's Crossing nearby. During the Third War, Prince Arthas purged Stratholme after learning its grain had been laced with the Plague of Undeath.

After Lordaeron fell, Scourge magic spread unchecked. The soil turned brown and rotten. Ordinary plants warped into colossal mushrooms, and orange mist settled over the valleys.

sections.title: A War on Three Fronts
sections.body:
Stratholme is the Scourge's southern seat of power in Lordaeron. Baron Rivendare commands it under the direction of the lich Kel'Thuzad. In the southeast, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade has fortified Tyr's Hand and assaults Stratholme's scarlet strongholds.

The Crusade's hatred reaches beyond the undead to any living traveler who crosses its borders. Farther north, the Mossflayer forest trolls of Zul'Mashar wage isolated, desperate campaigns amid the wider conflict.

sections.title: Bastions of the Living
sections.body: Watch your footing in the Eastern Plaguelands. The neutral Argent Dawn keeps Light's Hope Chapel in the far east, where Alliance and Horde champions can find shelter, supplies, and flight routes. Beyond the chapel, ruined watchtowers mark Lordaeron's lost defenses: Crown Guard, Eastwall, Northpass, and Plaguewood.

faq.q: What caused the sky and trees to look so sick?
faq.answer: The Cult of the Damned's Plague of Undeath left its mark across the land. After the Third War, its necromantic magic blighted the earth, changed local wildlife, and filled the air with unnatural orange smog. Forests twisted into fungal groves such as the Plaguewood.

faq.q: Where can I find a safe haven or flight path here?
faq.answer: Light's Hope Chapel, on the zone's eastern edge, is the main sanctuary. The Argent Dawn maintains it and offers flight paths to Undercity, Ironforge, Chillwind Camp, and the Hinterlands for Alliance and Horde travelers.

faq.q: Who controls the city of Stratholme?
faq.answer: War divides Stratholme. Baron Rivendare rules most of its burning ruins for Kel'Thuzad, while the Scarlet Crusade holds an aggressive garrison in the western district. There, it wages a bloody siege against the undead.

faq.q: Why is the Scarlet Crusade hostile to outside adventurers?
aliases: why does scarlet crusade attack me
faq.answer: The Scarlet Crusade's zealotry and paranoia grew after Lordaeron fell and the Silver Hand fractured. Its members believe outsiders carry the plague or consort with the undead, so they attack those who approach strongholds such as Tyr's Hand.

faq.q: What happened to the town of Darrowshire?
faq.answer: During the Third War, Scourge forces led by the death knight Marduk the Black and the ghoul Horgus the Ravager attacked Darrowshire. Paladin Davil Crokford and Captain Joseph Redpath fought valiantly, but necromancy corrupted Redpath's soul and made him slaughter his own people. Darrowshire now lies in haunted ruins.

angles.text: Lordaeron's fall weighs heavily on the Silver Hand. Stratholme is where Arthas turned to darkness, and Light's Hope Chapel saw a valiant last stand.
As an undead, you know the Eastern Plaguelands as the Scourge's birthplace and a frontline where the Forsaken strike against their former masters and the Scarlet zealots.
For the Alliance, you enter the Plaguelands on a solemn pilgrimage to reclaim and honor the devastated remnants of your former northern allies.
You can gather rare, volatile herbs in this blighted region, including Arthas' Tears, Plaguebloom, and Black Lotus.
Truesilver, Mithril, and Rich Thorium veins lie across the corrupted hillsides and dangerous valleys infested by the Scourge.
